<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**3** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **20** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6fe99f8634e7da14d1af67f97a3b6b3030bf70ba` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `75d1344fa04e5e3c682de5dfb38103831d021080` — the merge of head `288190cde77357eee227b6f17e121511a732fc3e` into base `6fe99f8634e7da14d1af67f97a3b6b3030bf70ba`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 75d1344fa04e5e3c682de5dfb38103831d021080 && git checkout 75d1344fa04e5e3c682de5dfb38103831d021080
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6fe99f8634e7da14d1af67f97a3b6b3030bf70ba 288190cde77357eee227b6f17e121511a732fc3e && git checkout -B drift-repro 6fe99f8634e7da14d1af67f97a3b6b3030bf70ba && git merge --no-ff 288190cde77357eee227b6f17e121511a732fc3e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6fe99f8634e7da14d1af67f97a3b6b3030bf70ba
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `34c30195fcde0fbcc5bff2f50bbd80a295e5fe03`
Local-runs: none

Read at 2026-11-02T14:04Z from the net diff against `main` (merge-base `57cde8cb`, 5 files, +362/-7), card #29241 (body, triage 6575529488, claims 6576283748 and 6576374454, dev report 6578737095), the PR body, and the head's check-runs. Nothing was built, run or re-run. Every claim below is either read from code at the head or reasoned from the PR's own base and head measurements, and it says which.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The seam: right.** `normalizeNumericStringRow` now writes `String(value)` for a `number` or `boolean` on a `BOUNDED_STRING_FIELD_TYPES` field. The field scope is the numeric half's (`isInReadonlyScope(…, 'include')`: readonly included, `SKIP_FIELDS` and non-readonly `system` excluded). The written string is exactly the `s` that the string arm's `maxLength`, `minLength`, `valueDomain` and format checks read (`record-validator.ts` ~1286). Strings, `null`, a missing key, objects, arrays, `bigint` and every type outside the set fall through unchanged.
2. **Doors: no door is left half-applied.** I read each one at the head:
   - `insert()` calls the seam at engine.ts:15391. `insertMany()` is `insert(rows)` (16737).
   - `update()` calls it at 16828, ahead of the by-id and predicate dispatch, so `driver.update`, `driver.updateMany` and `updateByIdExpecting` all receive the rewritten payload.
   - The `validate()` dry run calls it at engine-validate.ts:158, and `validateInsertValues` at record-validator.ts:2164.
   - REST create, PATCH and batch, import, and the flow `create_record`/`update_record` nodes all reach the engine through these methods.
   - The only direct `driver.create` calls outside the engine are testkits (`default-organization*.testkit.ts`) and the `packages/verify` conformance harness. None of them is a product writer.
   - Residuals, all accepted under the #20309 posture: a value written after the door is not rewritten. That covers a `before*` hook (the PR says so), write middleware, and a CEL-expression `defaultValue` on a text field whose result is a number. The CEL case is read from the `defaultValue` docblock and not measured. The spec refuses a non-string *literal* default at parse.
   - Gap: no test pins `validate()`. The objectql file's header says only that it "calls the same function". The changeset names `validate()` among the doors, so this is a nit for the follow-up.
3. **Ordering: right.** The rewrite runs first, before the middleware, the `callerKeys` snapshot, defaults, hooks, the readonly strip, the validator and the driver's unique check. All of them therefore see one image.
   - Formula fields are computed on read from the stored row, so they read the string.
   - Hooks now receive `"42"` where they received `42`. The forced edit to `protocol-save-notice-answer.test.ts` shows this is visible to hooks. It is the same accident class as the numeric half, and it is acceptable.
   - Because the rewrite runs before the driver's unique check, that check now compares the judged string. That is correct, but it is also what moves the accept set in item 5.
4. **The read-back type change on driver-memory (`42` becomes `"42"`) corrects an accident; it does not break a contract.**
   - The published stored shape of a text-family field is a string. The arm itself says: "A string type's stored shape is a string". `FieldSchema` types it so. SQLite already handed back `"42.0"`, so no reader could have relied on a raw number across drivers.
   - What answers differently now on driver-memory, read from code:
     - An equality or `$in` comparand `42` on a text field. mingo compares strictly, so it no longer matches newly written rows.
     - The comparand `"42"` now matches those rows.
     - `sort` and `min`/`max` order lexically instead of putting numbers first by BSON type order.
     - A formula or validation-rule expression now reads a string.
   - All four make the field behave as its declared type. None is a published surface.
   - Should-fix follow-up, not owed by this card: the filter door has no text-family comparand arm. `normalizeFilterComparandTypes` in `packages/spec/src/data/filter-comparand-type.ts` is not field-aware. So a *number comparand* on a text field still answers by driver. On driver-memory it misses the row. On SQLite, TEXT affinity matches `'42'`. The seat should file it.
5. **must-fix: the accept set does move, on unique-constrained text fields.** The PR, the changeset and the `Clause-②` measurement say "nothing is refused and nothing is newly admitted". That was measured on single writes only. The driver's unique key now compares the rewritten value. Reasoned from code (`uniqueKeyOf` is a `JSON.stringify` of the stored parts in `memory-unique-constraint.ts`) and from the PR's own base/head table. Not run.
   - **Narrowing, on both drivers.** Take a `unique` text field, insert `{ code: 42 }`, then `{ code: "42" }`.
     - On main: driver-memory keys `[42]` and `["42"]`; SQLite stores `'42.0'` and `'42'`. Both writes answer 201.
     - On head: both store `"42"`, so the second write is `409 DUPLICATE_RECORD`.
     - The same holds for `true` then `"true"`.
   - **Widening, on SQLite, on an empty table.** Insert `{ code: true }`, then `{ code: 1 }`.
     - On main: both store `'1.0'`, so the second write is 409.
     - On head: `'true'` and `'1'` are distinct, so both writes answer 201.
     - The same holds for `false`/`0`, and for `42` then `"42.0"`.
   - **Legacy rows.** A row stored on main (`'42.0'`, or a raw `42` on a driver-memory store with `persistence: 'file'`, `'local'` or an adapter) no longer collides with a new write of the same value.
   - The card's own business case names exactly the fields that carry `unique`: "a phone extension, a code, an external id".
   - **Each new answer is the one the validator's reading implies.** I judge the direction right. The declaration and the prose are what is wrong (see ②).
6. **Prose, should-fix.**
   - The PR's acceptance note says "driver-memory rows are process-lifetime". `InMemoryDriver` takes opt-in `persistence` (`file`, `local`, or a custom adapter; `memory-driver.ts` ~236). Persisted raw scalars outlive the change, as SQLite's `'42.0'` rows do.
   - The census covered objectql, rest, runtime, service-automation and dogfood. Plugin suites (for example plugin-audit and service-messaging) were not under the probe. I spot-read the obvious text-typed value columns: `sys_audit_log.old_value`/`new_value` are written through `safeStringify`. I found no product number writer, but the census is not exhaustive.

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset `'@objectstack/objectql': patch`: right.** It is a fix in a released package. A non-protocol change ships `patch` even when it narrows, keeping the banner. `Metadata-protocol: none` is also right: no key, accepted value or metadata type that an author writes moves.
- **`Clause-②: no`: wrong. must-fix.** Item ① 5 shows a write sequence accepted on main that is refused at the head (narrowing, both drivers). On SQLite it also shows a sequence refused on main that is admitted at the head (widening). Under the closed pair, the line has to carry the narrowing arm:
  - `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` if the seat counts the SQLite de-collision as a widening;
  - otherwise `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`.
  - Either way the arm is BREAKING. It owes the changeset a BREAKING banner, the ADR-0087 disposition marker beside both declaration lines (`pnpm check:adr-0087-registration`), and a `Skills-docs:` line on the PR body. A narrowing arm also moves the review face to `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` (`--face narrowing`), so a TIER_DEFAULT PASS could not govern this head in any case.
- **The alternative is a ruling.** If the seat rules on the card that a state-dependent unique outcome between values the validator already reads as one string is outside Clause-②, plain `no` can stand. The prose "nothing is refused / nothing is newly admitted" in the PR body and the changeset (which ships as `CHANGELOG.md`) still has to be corrected to name the unique-collision change, and that ruling has to be on the card before a re-review.
- **Either path owes a pin:** one test of the unique-collision answer on the SQLite real-driver file the PR already adds.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **open_questions: the function name (`normalizeNumericStringValues` now also writes the string arm's reading).** Answer: **A, keep the name in this PR.** The docblock's `[#29241]` section names the second half, and a rename touches engine.ts call sites that other server cards serialise on. A rename (for example `normalizeJudgedScalarValues`) is optional future hygiene, not owed. If the seat wants it, it belongs on #29244, which edits the same file next.
- **Deviation: no driver-memory test pin.** Accepted. `scripts/check-driver-memory-census.mjs` and its ledger confine driver-memory test consumers to ruled files. The objectql recording-driver test pins what every driver receives (the string), and driver-memory stores what it receives (the base measurement). The real-driver pin is SQLite in `packages/rest`.
- **Deviation: PostgreSQL and MongoDB NOT MEASURED.** Accepted, with residual risk named. The engine now hands every driver a JS string, so no driver decides for new writes. What stays unmeasured is each driver's legacy rows (MongoDB keeps raw numbers and booleans as written) and their unique answer (①5). Neither blocks this card. The migration of legacy rows stays a separate card, as the PR says.
- **Deviation: runtime, service-automation and dogfood ran at `27920d0a` with a log-only probe, before the `origin/main` merge and the forced test edit.** Accepted as evidence for the census, not as head verdicts.
  - The delta to the head is main's own merged work (#29271 and others), plus one objectql test-file edit.
  - objectql and rest were re-run on the head, and the head's Test Core shards carry the CI verdict (see below).
  - CI's dogfood legs were **skipped by the path filter** ("Dogfood Regression Gate: satisfied — no shard was expected to run"). So the only dogfood reading of this stored-form change is the pre-merge local one. The seat should re-run it on the head if the card delta owes it at the head itself.
- **Out-of-scope findings.**
  - The string arm judges a `Date` or another class instance by `String(value)` while the raw object is stored. That is the same judged≠stored class this card fixes. The seat should file a card for it; it is not this PR's.
  - Legacy SQLite `'42.0'`/`'1.0'` rows, and persisted driver-memory raw scalars: a migration card only if wanted.
  - The filter-door text comparand gap in ①4: should be filed.
- **Dev deviations "no assignee" and "no PR subscription":** relay rules, no contract bearing.
- **PR state.** The PR is a draft. Its author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay), so no out-of-relay login to note.
- **CI on the head:** all 48 check-runs completed: 35 success and 13 skipped, with 0 failures and 0 in progress. Test Core 1–8/8, the Test Core aggregate, Type Check (workspace, source, consumer, debt ledger), Build Core, every Lint leg, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard and PR-body guards all passed. Skipped by the path filter: the UI legs, the Dogfood shards and Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), and the opt-in legs. The CI gates are green, so this FAIL rests on ② alone.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`

Scope: packages/objectql/src/validation/record-validator.ts, packages/objectql/src/validation/record-validator.text-scalar-value.test.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-data-text-scalar-value.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/protocol-save-notice-answer.test.ts, .changeset/29241-text-field-scalar-stored-string.md + packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-validate.ts, packages/objectql/src/number-comparand-declared-type-door.ts, packages/spec/src/data/filter-comparand-type.ts, packages/spec/src/data/filter-number-comparand-declared-type.ts, packages/spec/src/data/filter-text-comparand.ts, packages/drivers/driver-memory/src/memory-driver.ts, packages/drivers/driver-memory/src/memory-unique-constraint.ts, content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx, content/docs/protocol/objectql/query-syntax.mdx

Round 2, on the narrowing face. Supersedes record 6579147685 (TIER_DEFAULT FAIL on head `34c30195`, which failed on the declaration alone and passed the code). Nothing was built, run or re-run; every statement about behaviour below is read from the code at the head or from the PR's own base and head measurements, and says which. The dispatch brief's conclusions were not an input.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The seam: right.** `normalizeNumericStringRow` (record-validator.ts) now takes a `number` or `boolean` (`isStringReadScalar`) beside a string, and on a field whose type is in the spec's `BOUNDED_STRING_FIELD_TYPES` writes `String(value)`, the exact `s` the string arm reads for `maxLength`, `minLength`, `valueDomain` and the email/url/phone formats. The string half is unchanged (`isJudgedNumberType` then `parseNumericString`). Field scope is the numeric half's, `isInReadonlyScope(name, def, 'include')`: readonly reached, `SKIP_FIELDS` and non-readonly `system` not. Strings, `null`, a missing key, objects, arrays, `bigint`, `Date`, and every type outside the set fall through by reference (`out ?? row`). Copy-on-write per row and per array holds.
2. **Doors: every engine write passes the seam, read at the head.** `insert()` calls it at engine.ts 15391 (after `normalizeBlankTypedValues`), `update()` at 16828 ahead of the by-id, `updateByIdExpecting` and `updateMany` dispatch, the `validate()` dry run at engine-validate.ts 158, `validateInsertValues` at record-validator.ts 2164. The remaining direct `driver.create` / `driver.update` sites in engine.ts (`createWithAutonumberResync` 8863 and 8919, the hook-context update at 18204, the `bulkCreate` fan-out at 16477 and 16480) all receive a row that already passed one of those two doors. REST create, PATCH, batch, import and the flow record nodes reach the engine through them. Residual, accepted under the #20309 posture the docblock states: a value a `before*` hook or write middleware writes after the door is its own.
3. **Ordering: right.** The rewrite runs before the middleware, the caller snapshot, defaults, hooks, the readonly strip, the validator and the driver's unique check, so every reader sees one image. Hooks now receive `"42"` where they received `42` (the forced edit to `protocol-save-notice-answer.test.ts` is that effect made visible; moving the vehicle field to `json` keeps the hook's raw-number case intact). Formulas, aggregation `min`/`max`/`groupBy`, search and the memory driver's filter all read the string.
4. **Accept-set changes the diff implies, each judged:**
   - Single write on a text-family field: unchanged. The arm's verdict reads `s`, which is byte-equal to what is now stored. Right.
   - `unique` text-family field, both drivers: `42` then `"42"` (and `true` then `"true"`) was two rows, is now `409 UNIQUE_VIOLATION` on the second. Read from `uniqueKeyOf` (`JSON.stringify` of the stored parts, memory-unique-constraint.ts 499-518) and from the PR's base/head table; pinned by two REST tests. A narrowing, and the right one: the validator read both writes as one value, and now the constraint does too.
   - `unique` text-family field, SQLite only: `true` then `1`, `false` then `0`, `42` then `"42.0"` were 409 (both bound as REAL/integer and spelled `'1.0'`/`'0.0'`/`'42.0'` by TEXT affinity), now two rows. A widening, and the right one: they are different strings under the spec's reading. Pinned by two REST tests. driver-memory admitted both before and still does.
   - Read-back type on driver-memory: `42` becomes `"42"`. The published stored shape of the family is a string (types.mdx: SQL `TEXT`, MongoDB `String`; the arm: "a string type's stored shape is a string"), so this corrects an accident and publishes nothing new.
   - Filter answers (ruled on in ④): `{ title: 42 }` at head matches no row on either driver; `{ title: "42" }` matches every row written as 42 or "42". Right as a consequence of the write door; the comparand gap is the filter door's and pre-existing.

5. **No public surface moves.** No export, type, Zod schema or metadata key changes; `packages/spec` is untouched; the one new function (`isStringReadScalar`) is module-private.
6. **Prose in the tree, should-fix (not blocking).** Two sentences at the head still carry round 1's claim that the seat ruled false: the `[#29241]` docblock section in record-validator.ts ("Nothing is refused or newly admitted: only the stored form of a value the arm already admits changes") and the header of `record-validator.text-scalar-value.test.ts` ("Nothing is refused and nothing is newly admitted"). Round 1's must-fix named only the PR body and the changeset, and both are corrected; these two comments should say what the changeset says (single-write answer unchanged; the `unique` answer moves). Fix them in the follow-up, or when #29244 next edits the file.

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset `'@objectstack/objectql': patch`: right.** A fix in a released package; AGENTS Post-Task step 3: a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition.
- **`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` in the PR body and the changeset: right**, and it is the arm the seat ruling 6579176393 amended the claim to. ①4 shows the narrowing (both drivers) and the widening (SQLite), so `yes` with the `(narrowing)` arm is the one well-formed spelling under the closed pair.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none`: right.** No key, accepted value or metadata type an author writes moves.
- **BREAKING banner: present, and it names the FROM → TO case** (`{ code: 42 }` then `{ code: "42" }`: two rows → `409 UNIQUE_VIOLATION`), the caller's one-line fix, and the SQLite widening in the other direction. The code name matches what the REST test asserts and what engine.ts 8773 documents (`UNIQUE_VIOLATION` / 409).
- **ADR-0087 marker: exactly one, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, honest.** No metadata key, export or type moves, so `objectstack migrate meta` has nothing to rewrite and no tombstone is owed; the body's "send the string once, or update the existing row" is a behavioural note, not a code-rewrite prescription. The gate (`Lint · CI, release & engine gates`) is green on the head, and the dev reports `check-adr-0087-registration --base origin/main` exit 0 with the `[BREAKING+bang+clause-②-narrowing]` signal set.
- **PR title `fix(objectql)!:` carries the bang** and matches the changeset summary's `!`, so the gate's three signals (bang, banner, narrowing arm) agree.
- **`Skills-docs: none — …` line: present and true** as far as the tree shows: no file under `skills/**`, `.claude/skills/**` or `content/docs/**` teaches writing a number or boolean into a text-family field or how `unique` compares `42` with `"42"`; the types page already states the family's stored shape.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **open_questions — the function name** (`normalizeNumericStringValues` now carries the string arm's half). **Answer: A, keep the name.** The docblock's `[#29241]` section names the second half, and a rename touches engine.ts call sites other server cards serialise on. Optional hygiene for #29244, which edits the same file next; not owed.
- **Round 1 must-fixes, all three met at the head:** (1) the declaration in body and changeset now reads `yes (narrowing)` with banner, marker and `Skills-docs:` line; (2) the "nothing is refused / nothing is newly admitted" prose in the body and the changeset is replaced by the single-write / unique-answer distinction (the two in-tree comments in ①6 remain, should-fix); (3) the unique answer is pinned: four REST tests on SQLite (two 409, two 201/201) and one objectql recording-driver test.
- **Deviation: no driver-memory test pin.** Accepted. The driver-memory census gate admits only ruled consumers; the recording-driver test pins what every driver receives, and the real-driver pin is SQLite in `packages/rest`.
- **Deviation: PostgreSQL and MongoDB NOT MEASURED.** Accepted with the residual named: the engine now hands every driver a JS string, so no driver decides for new writes; what stays unmeasured is each backend's legacy rows and their unique answer. Not this card's.
- **Deviation: runtime, service-automation and the round-1 dogfood reading ran at `27920d0a` with a log-only probe in objectql's dist.** Accepted as census evidence, not as head verdicts. The head's verdicts are the check-runs below plus the dev's round-2 dogfood reading at `926fa801` (393 files, no failures; CI's dogfood shards were skipped by the path filter, so that local reading is the only dogfood reading of this head).

### ④ Design judgment

**The narrowing against the published spec on `main`.** The spec declares a text-family field's stored value to be a string (types.mdx: `TEXT` on every SQL dialect, `String` on MongoDB; the record validator: "a string type's stored shape is a string; everything below is a bound, a domain or a format"), and `unique` as a constraint over stored values. On `main` the validator read `42` as `"42"` and admitted it, while the driver stored the raw scalar, so a `unique` column held two rows for one value on both drivers, and SQLite refused two different values (`true`, `1`) because its affinity spelled them alike. Neither answer was declared anywhere; both were the judged ≠ stored accident reaching the constraint. The narrowing takes no declared capability away at the consumer: it makes the spec's own refusal (one value, one row) real, and the SQLite widening is the same reading applied to values the spec says are different. Pinned on the real driver in both directions. I tried to break the design on `-0` (`"0"`), `1e21` (`"1e+21"`), `NaN`, a `password` or `valueDomain` field, a readonly text field, `update` by predicate, `updateByIdExpecting` under a precondition, the autonumber resync path and the `bulkCreate` fan-out: in each case the stored string is byte-equal to the `s` the arm judged, and the rewritten row is the one every later reader gets. No must-fix.

**The filter measurement the dev reported (two rows, 42 and "42"; base `{ title: 42 }` matched the raw-42 row on both drivers; head it matches nothing on both, `{ title: "42" }` matches both rows). Ruling: (b), a pre-existing filter-door gap this PR exposes, not a regression it introduces.** Argued from the published filter contract and the code:

- The filter contract has two kinds of door. The comparand-TYPE door (`filter-comparand-type.ts`, #7872 ruling) judges the comparand's JS type alone: `number` is one of the six accepted literal types on any field. The field-aware declared-type doors live at the engine's single filter seam (`number-comparand-declared-type-door.ts`, engine.ts 1300-1352) and exist for number fields (#20351: a numeric string is narrowed to its number, a non-numeric string, boolean, `Date` or array is refused `INVALID_FILTER`/400), boolean fields (#21333), temporal fields (#8690, and the docs' sentence "the same normalization is applied on write, on read, and to every filter comparand, so the two sides of a comparison can never disagree") and the text operators (#15661; `$icontains` refuses a non-string comparand, #18113). For a scalar comparand under equality or `$in` on a text-family field there is no arm: a `number` or `boolean` comparand passes to the driver as written. That absence is on `main`, in files this PR does not touch.
- What `main` did with it was never a declared answer. driver-memory hands the predicate to mingo, which compares strictly, so `{ title: 42 }` matched only a row holding the JS number 42, i.e. only a row produced by the accident this card fixes; it never matched a row written as `"42"`. SQLite binds the comparand as a REAL and TEXT affinity spells it `'42.0'`, so `{ title: 42 }` matched only rows the same accident had stored as `'42.0'`, missed every `'42'` row, and would match a row a client wrote as the string `"42.0"`. The "found its row" on `main` was the write-side accident reflected on the read side, driver-shaped on both drivers, not a capability the spec published. The published stored shape is a string, and the published filter posture for a comparand the column cannot hold is a loud door, never a driver-decided answer.
- What this PR changes on the read side is only that every text row is now stored as the spec says, so the missing arm is visible to the client that relied on the accident. That client's symmetric filter `{ title: "42" }` now matches on both drivers, and its read-back is `"42"` on both; before, neither held across drivers.
